title: Iulii Firmici Iunioris Mathesis
shelf_note: A humanist-cursive manuscript of Firmicus Maternus, Mathesis book VI (sample nativities of Demosthenes, Homer and Plato). It matches the title and the '15th century' date. No tradition or collection is set, so there is nothing to contradict.
structure_note: The number at the head of the leaf, 'VI', is the running book number (Liber VI), not a folio, but the OCR records it as <page-num>VI</page-num>. Running book numbers read as page numbers would explain most of the 49 backsteps and 46 repeats (a misread furniture artefact, not a scan splice). structure.pages_translated is 0 against pages_translated_field 302, so one of the counters is wrong (E2).

pages.layout: single column of humanist cursive; red marginal rubrics in the left margin (pro mendicis, pro cecis, pro oratoribus, Natale demosthenis/poetae/Homeri/platonis); bracket marks and faint show-through; book open with the facing leaf edge at right

'signum Tauri' (Saturn in Taurus) misread as 'pignu iouis'; a planetary position in Demosthenes' chart is lost

tr_errors.source: An animo mesto cupiditatis ardore prorepserit iungit uxores facit
tr_errors.english: with a sorrowful mind it creeps forth in the ardour of desire and brings about marriages
tr_errors.problem: the manuscript says this conjunction joins men to their sisters as wives with incestuous desire; the English gives an innocuous, invented sense
the leaf reads 'signum tauri'; the English carries the misread, and a note calls the manuscript 'obscure' when it is clear

tr_errors.source: Sol uero in equo constitutus signo
tr_errors.english: the Sun is placed in the sign of the horse
tr_errors.problem: built on a misread (the leaf has Capricorn, as far as can be read), and a note then claims the sign is 'probably Sagittarius'; the Sun's position in Homer's chart is wrong

tr_errors.source: ut Martis et Arepiteris pugnasque metuenda tonitrua
tr_errors.english: sets forth the battles of Mars and of the gods and the fearful thunders
tr_errors.problem: 'and of the gods' is invented to cover the garble ('Martios strepitus' = the din of Mars), and the note offers Jupiter

tr_errors.source: homeri diuini in illis heroici carminis fecit interprete
tr_errors.english: Such a nativity made Homer the divine interpreter of heroic song.
tr_errors.problem: loses 'Iliacum': Homer as the interpreter of Iliadic heroic song

tr_errors.english: set in the place before it
tr_errors.problem: the leaf has 'in the fifth place'; the English invents a position

book_verdict: The manuscript is the right one and the OCR is broadly of this leaf, but several meaning-changing misreads (the incest clause, Saturn in Taurus, the Sun's sign in Homer's chart) reach the English. Three notes give the misreads false authority: they call a clear reading 'obscure', suggest Sagittarius and offer Jupiter.
